subject: Evidence request: RBAC matrix, SAML assertion samples, SCIM delta snapshot
messages:
From: Danielle Ortiz <d.ortiz@carebridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask: access control evidence for SOC2/SIG

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. As part of our SOC 2 and SIG review, the security team asked us to collect a short set of artifacts focused on access control and provisioning. Can you provide the following by next Friday (11/06):

- A snapshot of SCIM delta logs covering the last 30 days (CSV or similar).
- 3 anonymized SAML assertion samples that show typical login flows (including NameID and common attributes).
- Current RBAC role matrix (who has admin-level roles vs. product-level roles) and a short justification for any roles that are broader than least privilege.

If you need a template for the RBAC justification or prefer to deliver a summary + a spreadsheet, that's fine. Also: do you have any PII in assertion attributes we should redact before delivery?

Appreciate it — Danielle
Security Program Manager
CareBridge


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Ortiz <d.ortiz@carebridge.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: access control evidence for SOC2/SIG

Danielle — thanks for the clear list. We'll own delivery and can meet the 11/06 target. Quick plan: 

1) Jonas will pull the SCIM delta export and SAML assertion samples and redact any PII.
2) Soojin and I will assemble the RBAC role matrix and include per-role justification (short bullets) for any role with elevated privileges.
3) We'll upload artifacts to a share link and send a short manifest with what was redacted.

A few clarifying Qs:
- For SCIM deltas, do you prefer a single combined CSV or a split by user/change type? Either is fine for us; combined is usually easier for your auditors.
- On SAML assertions, if you need AuthnContext or audit timestamps included, let us know — we can include the raw fields but will mask email addresses.

Action items: Jonas — can you estimate whether the SCIM/SAML exports will need a partial retention run (we might need to rehydrate logs)?
Jonas and Soojin — I put CareBridge in the delivery column for the 11/06 target.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: RBAC-justification-template.md (template for role-level notes)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Ortiz <d.ortiz@carebridge.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: access control evidence for SOC2/SIG

Marissa / Soojin / Danielle — quick technical update and attached stubs.

- SCIM delta: I pulled a 30-day delta from the provisioning pipeline (2026-10-04 to 2026-11-03). File: scim_delta_snapshot.csv (contains timestamp, change_type, username_hash, source, actor_role). We hashed usernames and removed email local parts as requested.
- SAML samples: gathered three typical assertion payloads (interactive SSO, federated SAML from partner, and a JIT service account flow). File: saml_assertion_samples.zip (each XML is redacted: NameID is a pseudonym, email addresses masked, unique IDs preserved).
- RBAC matrix: created v2 of the matrix (rbac_role_matrix_v2.xlsx). I flagged five roles that were originally broader (product_admin_global); included a short rationale and proposed scope-reduction where feasible.

Notes / caveats:
- The SCIM export omits raw email addresses (we replaced them with stable hashed ids) and excludes MFA events (those are in a separate auth log). If auditors need the MFA timeline we can provide an exported slice but will need approval from Security Ops.
- The SAML assertion containing kerberos attributes has an internal artifact (authnInstant) that references an internal timestamp format; I left it unchanged but annotated it in the manifest.

I uploaded the three artifacts to the restricted Drive folder and added a manifest.txt describing redactions. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/requests/CB-4567 (restricted; access granted to your security group).

-- Jonas
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: saml_assertion_samples.zip (3 XMLs, redacted), scim_delta_snapshot.csv, rbac_role_matrix_v2.xlsx, manifest.txt

From: Danielle Ortiz <d.ortiz@carebridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: access control evidence for SOC2/SIG

Thanks, team — that looks good and the restricted drive is accessible. A couple of follow-ups before we mark this closed with our auditor: 

- Please provide a one-paragraph justification for each of the five flagged roles explaining why the role is necessary and the plan/timeline to reduce scope where you proposed changes. A short owner + ETA is sufficient.
- For the SCIM CSV, can you add a change_type filter column note in the manifest (the auditor wants to easily show adds vs. modifies vs. deletes).
- Confirm that saml_assertion_samples.zip contains no unredacted PII (if there are any doubts, create a ZIP with the same filenames and a _redacted suffix).

If it's easier, deliver the role justifications as a single consolidated file (RBAC-justifications-summary.md) and drop it into the same restricted folder. We'll confirm acceptance once we verify redaction and the change_type labels.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Danielle
